p: Dundee Road is part of the Slough Trading Estate, a huge business area to the west of the town centre, so it's easy to reach from the M4 and the A4 without getting snarled up in the middle of town. It's busy with lorries during the working week, so give yourself a few extra minutes at peak times.

Slough has had its fair share of jokes thanks to The Office, which was set in a fictional paper company in the town. But there's more to the place than that. The astronomer William Herschel lived in Slough and made his famous telescopes here, and Herschel Park, a pretty Regency-era park with lakes and woodland, is named in his honour. It's a lovely, peaceful spot that a lot of visitors miss.

For proper woodland, Burnham Beeches, just to the north, is an ancient woodland nature reserve with huge old pollarded trees, ponds and easy paths. It's spectacular in autumn when the leaves turn gold.
The Elizabeth line now runs through Slough station, making it simpler than ever to get here from central London or Reading, and buses connect the station with the trading estate.

If your gang still has energy left after the trampolines and Windsor, Legoland Windsor Resort is just down the road, though it's a full day out in its own right. Eton, across the Thames from Windsor, is lovely for a quieter stroll along its high street, and the Jubilee River walking route offers a peaceful amble by the water.
Mix and match, and Slough suddenly looks like a pretty decent base for a family weekend.
Just remember that the Windsor area gets very busy in summer, so earlier starts are your friend.
